data.narrative:
Critical Energy, a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Spencer Jackson, has raised $22M to date. The target company operates within a sector encompassing one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $22M as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage transitions, the method implies a valuation of $55M. Peer-median triangulation could not be performed; while eight same-sector peers exist in the Climate & Energy universe, none met narrow filtration criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), and a broad all-sector median would introduce unwarranted noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $47M to $63M, centered on $55M. This range is derived from stage-progression analysis alone, with 15% sensitivity bands applied to account for methodological uncertainty. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for Critical Energy's specific market conditions, the absence of directly comparable peer data at seed stage, and variability in climate-tech investor appetite. Additional publicly available valuation evidence or an expanded private peer set at the same stage would materially improve precision.
